text:
alex: Heads up — I discovered a chunk of late telemetry for Dedicated instance usage between 2026-02-28 and 2026-03-02. Ingestion stalled due to an S3 list latency/timeout cascade. We need a backfill + recompute of the daily aggregates used by the console (quotas, billing, per-route dashboards). Thoughts on safe plan?

maria: Are the raw events intact in the usual parquet path? If yes we can do an idempotent replay/upsert into telemetry_agg. Key is to generate a manifest and ensure partition-level idempotency.

jon: Agree but want to avoid hammering the OLAP DB or the materialized view refresh. Run on archival Spark cluster with low priority. Ramp gradually (5% of date partitions first) and throttle writes.

sarah: Also recommend a canary: recompute only the last 24h and diff against current MV, if delta > 1% fail and investigate. We should add checksum and row-count comparisons.

alex: Draft plan: 1) identify affected event_date partitions 2) generate replay manifest 3) run spark replay job with upsert semantics into db.telemetry_agg 4) run validation (checksums/rowcounts/cost sanity) 5) swap materialized view or apply patch. We'll gate console reads with a feature flag during swap.

alex: Proposed spark command snippet:
```bash
# generate manifest
python tools/replay_manifest.py --start 2026-02-28 --end 2026-03-02 --out s3://redwood-replay/manifests/replay-20260228-0302.json

# run replay (example)
spark-submit \ \ 
  --master yarn \ \ 
  --conf spark.executor.cores=4 \ \ 
  --conf spark.sql.shuffle.partitions=200 \ \ 
  jobs/replay_recompute.py --manifest s3://redwood-replay/manifests/replay-20260228-0302.json \ \ 
  --target db.telemetry_agg --mode upsert --idempotent-key event_id
```

jay: (typo — that was me, ignore)

jon: We should also add write throttling on the DB side (rate-limited connector) and use a small staging table that we swap into production after validation. No in-place heavy updates.

maria: Console UX note — while the recompute is running, panels that depend on daily aggregates should show a "recomputing" state and hide noisy alerts. I'll add a remote config flag telemetry.recompute_in_progress that the frontend can check.

alex: I'll add that flag. Also we should ensure billing/quotas pipeline is paused from emitting alerts until the recompute passes validation, otherwise customers will see wrong overages.

ops-bot: replay-runner scheduled replay-20260228-0302 at 2026-03-20T02:00:00Z on cluster archival-spark-02.

replay-runner: job replay-20260228-0302 created (id: r-20260320-07). First phase: manifest validation and checksum.

sarah: Retention/late-arrival policy discussion: maybe increase watermark to 48h for production to reduce frequent small backfills. But enforce a max_backfill_window = 7d so we don't let arbitrarily old data be replayed without review.

jon: +1. Also let's add a concurrency limit in the orchestration layer (max_parallel_replays = 2) so we don't create multiple heavy replays concurrently.

maria: I'll own the canary validation script. Plan to compare token counts, per-route request counts, and a small sample of full traces for semantic drift. If token delta or cost delta > 2% we halt.

alex: Ownership: alex -> manifest & orchestration, maria -> validation & console UX, jon -> infra throttling & staging swap, sarah -> runbook + retention policy. I'll open a short RFC and schedule the first canary run Tue 02:00 UTC.

jon: Please also add a rollback step in the runbook: if validation fails, abort swap and mark flag telemetry.recompute_failed with reason for the console.

maria: Will do. I'll also add a small dashboard to show per-partition progress and ETA so product can see when quotas will be consistent again.

alex: Cool. Thanks y'all — I'll post the RFC link here when created and tag the run when it's kicked off. :thumbsup: :party_parrot:
